newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Six killed by gunmen in northern Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Six killed by gunmen in northern Colombia.

text.p: At least six people were killed by suspected right-wing gunmen who dragged them out of their homes in a banana-growing region of northern Colombia, police said on Friday.
The victims, a woman and five men, were pulled into fields outside the town of Fundacion, in Magdalena province, and killed by masked gunmen late on Thursday, police said.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility, but police said the killings appeared similar to others committed in the region by right-wing death squads. At least 25 people have been killed so far this year.
Fundacion is located near the town of Aracataca, where Colombia's Nobel laureate Gabriel Garcia Marquez was born 70 years ago, on March 6, 1927.
The world-renowned author of "One Hundred Years of Solitude" has cited Colombia's seemingly uncontrolled levels of violence as one of the reasons he has decided to live in self-imposed exile abroad.

Hinting at the scope of the violence, a British priest in Calamar, a small town in Bolivar, a province that shares a border with Magdalena, said in an interview on national radio early on Friday that residents there had seen as many as 15 corpses floating down a river in the last week.
"No one knows why they're floating there," said the priest identified as John Mancy. "No one knows who killed them."
Colombia, a country torn by endemic levels of political and drug-related bloodshed, has the highest murder rate in Latin America, according to a World Bank report released earlier this week.
